blockers.description: F-04 (activate-tenant concurrency guard, 04-REVIEW.md WR-02): MySQL GET_LOCK/RELEASE_LOCK are session-scoped; Sequelize connection pooling means a naive implementation could silently run GET_LOCK and RELEASE_LOCK on different pooled connections, making the lock a no-op. Correct implementation requires pinning both calls to one connection via Sequelize's unmanaged-transaction-as-connection-affinity-handle technique, PLUS updating 7 existing test mocks in tests/activateTenant.test.js that currently stub createTargetConnection minimally. No real MySQL is available in this sandbox to empirically prove the lock actually prevents a real concurrent race — only mocked call-shape assertions are possible, which for a concurrency-correctness fix specifically gives false confidence if any detail is wrong.
blockers.workaround: Awaiting explicit user go-ahead before implementing. If approved: implement with the connection-pinning technique, add mocked tests for acquire/release/timeout paths, and explicitly document in the commit message and test file that real-concurrency behavior remains unverified in this sandbox (same convention as this repo's other RUN_*_INTEGRATION-gated live-DB tests).

decisions.decision: Recommended NOT executing Phase 7 as originally scoped, and NOT skipping it either — recommended rescoping it around the narrower goal above.
decisions.rationale: The full original Phase 7 (07-01 repeated clone-loop rehearsal to N clean attempts + 07-02 formal backup/restore/abort/reopen-on-legacy runbook + 07-03 product/POS/frontend deferred-domain register) is heavier ceremony than an incremental, non-hard-cutover rollout needs, and 07-03's original framing (product/POS/frontend) is now moot since v2.0 (Phases 8-11) already built that domain fresh, not via migration.
